title: Which homology 3-spheres bound homology 4-balls?
exact_target: Can a complete effective criterion decide which integral or rational homology three-spheres bound smooth homology four-balls with the same coefficients?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Fix coefficients $R=\mathbb Z$ or $R=\mathbb Q$; these give two
separate versions. A closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold
$Y$ is an $R$-homology sphere if
$H_i(Y;R)\cong H_i(S^3;R)$ for every $i$. It bounds an
$R$-homology ball if there is a compact connected oriented smooth
four-manifold $W$ with oriented boundary $\partial W\cong Y$ and
\[
               H_i(W;R)\cong H_i(D^4;R)\qquad\text{for all }i.
\]
In particular the positive-degree homology groups vanish, but
contractibility or trivial fundamental group is not required.

The problem asks for complete computable invariants deciding, from
a finite triangulation or equivalent finite description of $Y$,
whether such a smooth $W$ exists. Completeness means a necessary
and sufficient criterion; computability means an effective evaluation
and decision procedure that terminates on every allowed input.
A list of obstructions with no terminating sufficiency test does
not yet provide the requested decision.

The smooth convention follows the source's four-manifold examples
and smooth cobordism obstructions; replacing it by arbitrary
topological fillings changes the problem. In the rational version
torsion in integral homology is allowed. An integral homology ball
is automatically a rational one, but the converse need not hold.
Both the coefficient ring and the filling category must remain fixed
throughout an instance.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can a complete effective criterion decide which integral or rational homology three-spheres bound smooth homology four-balls with the same coefficients?
